page: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64g-480s is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and SHA_NI. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 480 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in single-core operations, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Text processing via Geekbench and text generation using a small 135M parameter LLM model also achieve top-tier ratings. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range, as demonstrated by Geekbench multi-core scores and Passmark database operations. However, prompt processing for medium-sized 7B parameter LLM models is a relative bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC cores, high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU, and integrated NVMe storage, this server offers a balanced resource profile for memory-intensive workloads. It is well-suited for database hosting, memory-cached web serving, software compilation, and text-processing pipelines. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution without resource contention, making it a reliable option for production environments requiring stable memory capacity and moderate multi-threaded compute power.
